overall_summary: The channel FACTVERSE sees its strongest performance when combining extreme space phenomena with high-stakes survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') or highly visual, bizarre planetary conditions (e.g., burning ice, supersonic rubies, coal-dark planets). Conversely, generic psychology facts and repetitive brain-trick videos struggle heavily to gain traction, often stalling under 50 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Survival in Extreme Space Environments ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (949 views) and 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' (492 views) significantly outperform standard factual statements.
winning_patterns.action: Frame future space facts as hypothetical, high-stakes survival scenarios where the viewer is the main character.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,025 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) show high view counts and strong engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on extreme planetary physics, using highly contrasting sensory concepts (e.g., burning ice, dark light, supersonic gems) in the titles and hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' yielded only 5 to 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause the production of generic cognitive psychology and brain-hack content unless it can be tied to a highly unusual neurological mystery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Passive Planetary Facts Without High Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Eyeball Planet That Could Harbor Life!' (31 views) and 'The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Metal!' (10 views) failed to capture interest compared to active survival framing.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely descriptive titles. Convert passive facts ('It rains metal') into active, dramatic scenarios ('What happens if you get caught in a liquid metal storm').

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Planet of Supersonic Ruby Rain?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a visual of falling through a glittering, beautiful sky: 'You are falling through clouds of pure, sparkling rubies. But this isn't a dream—it's a deadly trap.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the winds on planet HAT-P-7b blow these gemstone shards at over 5,000 miles per hour, meaning you'd be shredded by supersonic jewelry before you even hit the ground.
next_video.reason: Combines the highly successful 'What If You Fell Into...' survival framing with the proven high-performance concept of supersonic gemstone rain (from the 721-view ruby planet video).

experiment: Test a 'Cinematic Animal Survival' micro-story using the same first-person high-stakes framing (e.g., 'What If You Had to Survive a Night as a Tardigrade in Outer Space?') to see if the survival hook translates to biology.
